name: Atom layer selection
purpose: Decide whether reusable headless behavior belongs in Atom, an existing native element, Brick, a higher composition layer, or the application before composing a primitive.
decisionOrder: Start from the semantic and interaction job, not the desired appearance.
Use an existing native element when it already provides the complete reusable behavior contract.
Use an Atom primitive when reusable semantics, state, focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, portal, positioning, or compound composition are required.
Use Brick instead when the consumer needs a finished visual component; ordinary Brick applications should not import Atom directly.
Keep product workflows, page layout, content, routing, persistence, and analytics in higher layers.

selection.note: Choose Link for ordinary navigation and Pressable only for custom interactive surfaces.
Compose Toolbar only when grouped controls require toolbar keyboard behavior.

selection.use: NavList, NavigationMenu, Breadcrumb, BottomNavigation, Tabs, or Pagination
selection.note: Select by the navigation relationship, not by visual resemblance.

selection.use: DropdownMenu from a visible button, ContextMenu from a contextual gesture, Menubar for persistent application command groups, or Menu as the shared direct/custom foundation
selection.note: Use Select or Listbox when choosing a form value and keep important contextual actions discoverable elsewhere.

selection.use: Tooltip for a brief hint or HoverCard for a richer passive preview
selection.note: Choose Popover when the content is interactive and visible native content when the information is essential.

selection.use: CheckboxGroup for independent form choices, RadioGroup for one visible form answer, Switch for an immediately applied on/off setting, Toggle for one pressed command, or ToggleGroup for related pressed commands
selection.note: Choose by semantics and application timing rather than visual shape.

selection.use: Slider for a general scalar or range adjusted by feel, or Rating for a short ordered score
selection.note: Choose NumberInput when exact typed entry matters and Progress when the value is read-only.

selection.use: Listbox for a visible composite list, Select for one collapsed fixed value, MultiSelect for several collapsed fixed values, or Combobox for editable filtering and optional valid free-form entry
selection.note: Choose RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup when short form choices should remain separate visible controls.

selection.use: NumberInput for exact numeric entry with stepping, OTPField for a short one-time code split across cells, or PasswordToggleField for a revealable reusable secret
selection.note: Keep ordinary text and digit-like identifiers in Input.
Use a native file input when custom picker, drop, validation feedback, and selected-item behavior are unnecessary; always validate uploads again on the server.
Choose Button when asynchronous copy state and authored feedback are unnecessary.
Use inline content for contextual or durable feedback and AlertDialog when a response is required.
Keep an obvious tap or click path and choose Menu when many actions or discovery make swipe unsuitable.
Choose Accordion for several coordinated sections or Dialog for a modal task.

selection.use: Table for read-oriented comparison, DataGrid for flat two-dimensional keyboard navigation or row selection, or TreeGrid for hierarchical interactive rows
selection.note: Keep sorting, editing, filtering, resizing, and virtualization application-composed and preserve full logical indexes when windowing.

selection.use: Tree for one primary item column or TreeGrid for several navigable columns
selection.note: Choose Accordion when branches contain general disclosure content rather than selectable items.
Choose List for a static set and add virtualization only when scale justifies its focus and accessibility cost.
Use Image when loading fallback is also required and keep all media semantics on the child.

selection.use: Avatar for a named entity or Badge for a short contextual count or status
selection.note: Keep essential identity visible and use Progress for ongoing completion rather than status text.

selection.use: Label for one standalone native control or Field.Label for coordinated control, description, error, and state wiring
selection.note: Use Fieldset for a group of controls.

selection.use: Progress for determinate or indeterminate completion
selection.note: Choose the native meter element for a stable measurement, Slider for user adjustment, or Toast for a short nonblocking update.
Prefer visible text when it benefits everyone and use aria-hidden rather than VisuallyHidden for decorative content.

selection.use: Direction together with the matching native dir attribute
selection.note: Provider mirrors Atom behavior but never replaces browser text-direction semantics; prefer a component's local dir prop only for an intentional nested override.

selection.intent: ordinary blocking task, form, or information surface
selection.note: Choose AlertDialog for an urgent consequential choice, Drawer for a side sheet, or Popover for a compact attached panel.
Application work should prefer the purpose-built modal-family components.

selection.intent: scrollable viewport with owned scrollbar behavior
selection.note: Keep ordinary document scrolling native.
Use a native img when loading state and fallback composition are unnecessary.
Choose Collapsible for one independent disclosure and Tabs for one shared switching panel.
Choose NavList or an interactive collection primitive when items navigate, select, or activate.

rules.statement: Keep Atom guidance and compositions headless; do not add visual recipes, color, theme, product copy, or application layout policy.
Preserve native semantics and behavior unless Atom explicitly owns the added reusable contract.
Do not rebuild focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, portal, positioning, or controlled-state behavior already owned by an Atom primitive.
When building with Brick, consume Brick public components and let Brick consume Atom rather than importing both layers directly.

nativeFallback.check: Search Atom's manifest, public exports, and related component guides for the required behavior before using a native fallback.
nativeFallback.use: Use the narrowest semantic native element only when no Atom primitive owns the behavior and no reusable state or interaction contract is being recreated.
nativeFallback.report: Record the missing primitive or intentional native choice so repeated gaps can be evaluated by Atom maintainers.

validation: Name the selected semantic and interaction job and its owning layer.
Confirm no visual or application policy entered the Atom composition.
Confirm the rendered elements, accessible names, state, focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, and RTL behavior that apply.
Record any native fallback and the Atom capability searched first.
